summary: Mystery line item: warmup surcharge allocated to merged subaccount on finalized invoice
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a finalized invoice containing a $3,225.67 line labeled 'warmup surcharge' that was charged to a subaccount that had been merged and decommissioned three days prior to invoice finalization. Impact: Customer is disputing the charge (USD 3,225.67) and has paused autopay for the invoice. They expect warmup credits to be consumed under the parent account or discarded for decommissioned keys. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod (us-east-1), hybrid reserved hours + hosted fallback during maintenance window (2026-03-05 02:00–04:00 UTC).

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Customer performed a subaccount merge on 2026-03-02 (subacct id: fc-042). Decommissioned API key rotated out same day.
2) Batch warmup jobs for a migrated model group ran on 2026-03-05 during maintenance; postbacks show warmup token hits across a mixed pool of reserved and hosted capacity.
3) Invoice finalized on 2026-03-08; line item shows warmup surcharge allocated to fc-042 (decommissioned) rather than parent org (fluxmind-prod).

Logs / artifacts attached: billing line export CSV (masked), postback delivery log snippet, consolidation job run id bk-20260305-11, screenshot of invoice line. Customer included a billing ledger export and a copy of the merge request JSON.

Customer expectation: Warmup-related charges should either be attributed to the active parent account or omitted if generated by decommissioned keys. Requesting provisional credit or removal pending reconciliation.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Miguel Ortega (Billing Eng): Pulled postback delivery logs; initial observation that postback processor used stale tag mapping for fc-042 during consolidation window. Opening INT ticket to trace tag-store rollback window.

2026-03-11 11:12 - SRE (Leah Chen): Found a cached tag mapping entry ttl not cleared after merge; cascade caused attribution to original subaccount for late-arriving postbacks. Confirmed with postback IDs bk-20260305-11:pb-9876.

2026-03-12 08:47 - Miguel Ortega (Billing Eng): Requested temporary provisional credit to offset customer while we fix attribution and re-run consolidation. Sent follow-up to Finance for manual adjustment.
2026-03-12 12:05 - Elena Park (Customer): Agreed to provisional credit while investigation proceeds. Asked for ETA on permanent fix and whether similar invoices may be impacted this cycle.
investigation_notes:
Findings to date:
- Postback processor accepted warmup events during maintenance window and wrote cost attribution using a tag lookup service.
- Tag-store had a TTL misconfiguration: merge operations set tombstone but TTL wasn't honoured by regional cache, so late postbacks (queue replay) used old mapping.
- Affected window: 2026-03-05 02:00–03:30 UTC.
- Counted warmup tokens: ~1.1M tokens attributed to fc-042; cost computed at hybrid warmup surcharge rate leading to USD 3,225.67.
Hypothesis: Cache invalidation race caused decommissioned subkey to remain addressable until cache TTL expired, causing misattribution for late-delivered postbacks.
Next steps:
1) Re-run consolidation pipeline for bk-20260305-11 with corrected tag mapping (pending safe run window).
2) Apply provisional credit of USD 3,225.67 to customer invoice (Finance ticket FIN-6120 opened).
3) Patch tag-store cache invalidation to expedite tombstone propagation (PR linked).
4) Audit other merges in March for similar symptoms (search job scheduled).
resolution: Pending - provisional credit requested and Finance ticket created. Engineering to re-run consolidation and deploy cache invalidation patch. Customer will receive a credit memo if consolidation removes the line. No permanent resolution applied yet.
